sections.html:
Nampa, in Canyon County, had an estimated 120,384 residents on July 1, 2025. That is 19.9 percent more than the April 2020 base of 100,414, and the town calls itself the Heart of the Treasure Valley. About 33.5 square miles lie inside city limits, with Interstate 84 running through.

Most households here own. The owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024 is 70.2 percent, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $370,800 against median gross rent of $1,420. Treat that median as a rough guide only, since your own house may sit well above or below it.

Growth means new subdivisions at the edges and older houses nearer the center. The two groups attract different buyers and need different repairs.

sections.h2: Railroad roots and the street grid
sections.html: The Oregon Short Line Railroad built through the site in the early 1880s on its way from Granger, Wyoming, to Huntington, Oregon, and the town grew up around it. Downtown streets run at an angle because they follow the tracks, which angle northwest to southeast. Union Pacific still uses the line.

Summers are hot and dry and winters cold with little rain. Heat and sun do most of the damage, with a hard freeze now and then. Yearly precipitation averages only about 11.4 inches, with December and January the wettest at roughly 1.4 inches each.

July highs average near 91 degrees and the record is 109. January lows average about 21 degrees, and the coldest day on record hit minus 26.

  • Air conditioners work hard, so buyers check how old yours is.
  • Roofing, fences and exterior paint age faster in strong sun.
  • Lake Ethel began as an irrigation reservoir, so some buyers ask whether a lot has irrigation service.

The Nampa School District covers most of the city, with Nampa, Skyview, Columbia and Union high schools. Part of town is in the Vallivue School District, home to Ridgevue High School, and a few blocks fall in West Ada. A buyer who cares about a particular school should check the district boundary, because the mailing address will not settle it.

The College of Western Idaho and Northwest Nazarene University are both in Nampa. Interstate 84 has four exits into town, Idaho 55 and Idaho 45 cross it, and ValleyRide runs local buses.

A sale does not require a permit, but unpermitted work can come up when a buyer or title company looks at the property. Nampa wants a residential building permit for a new home, an addition or a remodel. The City of Nampa Building Department answers permit questions at 208-468-5435.

Code Compliance and Community Relations takes complaints about property conditions. The city asks residents to report a neglected vacant home by calling 208-468-5473 or filing online.

  • Keep the yard and exterior of an empty house tidy, since neglected vacant homes draw complaints.
  • If you did work yourself, find out whether anyone pulled a permit, and say so if you do not know.
  • Hold on to any code notice. A buyer will want to see it.

Canyon County assesses and bills Nampa property on a calendar tax year. January 1 is the lien date, so the value that day is the one taxed.

DateWhat happens in Canyon County
JuneAssessment notices are mailed
Fourth Monday in JuneDeadline to appeal the assessed value
Second Monday in JulyCommissioners finish as the Board of Equalization
Fourth Monday in NovemberTax notices must be sent
December 20First half or full payment due
June 20Second half due

An appeal argues the property was worth less than the assessed amount on January 1. File in writing on a form from the Assessor's office by the fourth Monday in June. The Board of Equalization reviews the fairness and accuracy of the value. Whether you can afford the tax does not enter into it.

If you disagree with the board's decision, the next step is the State Board of Tax Appeals, and after that District Court. The county's Data Hub shows five years of assessment and tax history, which helps when you build your case. The assessment page on the Canyon County website explains the process.

Manufactured housing follows a tougher rule. If the first half of the tax is unpaid after December 20, that half is delinquent and the entire tax comes due in full. Call the treasurer's office at (208) 454-7354 with questions.

For any house with taxes owed, the title company will find the balance and pay it from your sale proceeds at closing. Tell the buyer up front so there are no surprises.

Anyone selling residential property with one to four units fills out a property condition disclosure form, as set out in Idaho Code section 55-2501 and the sections after it. You use it to describe material physical problems with the house.

Be specific. A furnace that fails in cold snaps, a roof that leaks at one corner, a room a past owner added without a permit: all of it goes on the form. Idaho Code 55-2508 has the standard wording.

A listing can bring a higher price for a house in good condition. A cash offer gives up some of that price in return for speed and certainty. What the house needs and how soon you must close should drive the choice.

  • List if the house is move-in ready and you can manage showings.
  • Go cash if repairs are beyond your budget, the house came to you by inheritance, or you are behind on payments.

We buy as-is, so you do not clean, repair or stage. We make an offer once we know the details, and a no from you costs nothing. We never quote a price in advance.

The process runs in order. You send the address and condition details, we make an offer, and if you accept a title company handles the closing and pays off any mortgage or taxes from the proceeds. Bring your latest tax bill and any code notices to the first conversation so the offer is accurate.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Nampa house?
faqs.a: Canyon County taxes are due December 20, and you may pay half by then and the other half by June 20. Tax notices go out by the fourth Monday in November.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal my Canyon County assessment?
faqs.a: The deadline is the fourth Monday in June. Notices are mailed in June, and the appeal is filed in writing on a form from the Assessor's office.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Nampa house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy as-is, including houses with open code issues. Tell us about any notices from Code Compliance so the offer reflects them.

faqs.q: Which Nampa school district is my house in?
faqs.a: Most of Nampa is in the Nampa School District. Parts are in Vallivue and a few blocks are in West Ada, so check the district map for your address before you list.
